<!--
Use an English Conventional Commit title and English body.
Motivation, Solution, Validation, and User impact and compatibility are required.
Include the optional sections only when they contain useful information.
Scale detail to the change; remove instructions and unfilled placeholders.
-->

## Motivation

<!--
Explain the concrete problem, its trigger or current behavior, and why the change
is needed. Include the goal and relevant constraints so a reader can understand
the reason without reconstructing a conversation or following external links.
-->

## Solution

<!--
Describe the meaningful changes as a few cohesive bullets, grouped by behavior.
Explain the resulting behavior and key design choices, including why the chosen
approach addresses the problem. Include affected interfaces, workflows, and
deliberate scope boundaries when useful. Do not reproduce the file list or the
implementation chronology. Link a decision record for deeper design discussion.
-->

## Validation

<!--
Use the table below or concise bullets. Name the check or command, its actual
result, and the behavior or candidate it covers; link evidence when useful.
Explain material checks not run. Distinguish local validation from PR CI and
release evidence. Record pending or failed checks accurately.
-->

| Check | Result | Coverage or evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <!-- Check or command --> | <!-- Actual result --> | <!-- Scope or evidence --> |

## User impact and compatibility

<!--
Describe effects on supported behavior, APIs, configuration, data, dependencies,
or development workflows as applicable. State any required migration or operator
action, remaining risk, and rollback/recovery considerations when relevant.
When no compatibility impact is expected, state the concrete basis briefly.
Do not substitute an unsupported blanket claim that the change is risk-free.
-->

## Reviewer notes

<!-- OPTIONAL: Name one to three non-obvious decisions, critical paths, or specific
questions where reviewer attention is useful. Identify remaining work and whether
it blocks merge; link separately tracked follow-up work when relevant. A follow-up
label does not waive acceptance conditions. Remove this section if unnecessary. -->

## References

<!-- OPTIONAL: Link relevant Issues, PRs, or decisions. Use closing keywords only
when this PR completes the Issue and closure is authorized. Otherwise use a
non-closing reference. Remove this section if no references are relevant. -->
